headline: Geopolitical Fog Greets Traders at Tuesday's Open as Oil Pressure and Tech Rotation Linger
body_html:
Wall Street returns from the Labor Day long weekend to a market shaped by escalating Middle East tensions. Houthi forces struck multiple Saudi cities over the extended break, wounding 73 people and rattling energy infrastructure, propelling Brent crude toward the $100-per-barrel threshold. Slower traffic through the Strait of Hormuz following Iranian retaliation threats has added a fresh supply-risk premium, while the Indian rupee logged its steepest single-session drop in more than a month on the oil shock.

The last completed session — Friday, September 4 — offered a split tape. Semiconductors led all sectors with a gain of 3.05%, powered by double-digit advances in memory and analog names, while Software surrendered 1.25% as automation and design software stocks absorbed sharp selling. Breadth was modestly constructive at 301 advancers versus 241 decliners across the 545-stock universe, though the gap between sector winners and losers was unusually wide.

Into Tuesday's open, traders will weigh whether Friday's chip-led momentum can offset geopolitical headwinds. Gold is nudging higher as investors eye upcoming U.S. inflation data, and one closely watched technology ETF has emerged as a potential bellwether for the durability of the broader bull market. Energy volatility and software weakness are the two pressure points to monitor at the bell.

briefs.headline: Houthi Strikes on Saudi Cities Deepen Gulf Risk Premium
briefs.body: Houthi forces attacked four Saudi cities over the holiday weekend, wounding 73 people and disrupting energy facilities. The strikes have driven oil prices to multi-week highs, with Brent approaching the psychologically significant $100-per-barrel level. Analysts are questioning why prices have not already eclipsed that mark despite meaningful supply disruptions.

briefs.headline: Hormuz Slowdown Adds Another Layer to Oil Supply Anxiety
briefs.body: Vessel traffic through the Strait of Hormuz has decelerated after Iran threatened retaliation for prior U.S. military actions in the region. The chokepoint handles a substantial share of global crude flows, and any sustained slowdown would tighten an already strained supply picture heading into the autumn demand season.

briefs.headline: Semiconductor Names Dominate Friday's Leaderboard
briefs.body: The semis sector surged 3.05% on Friday, the strongest showing of any group in the universe. Sandisk climbed 11.9%, Semtech advanced 9.22%, and KLA Corp and Marvell Technology each rose more than 7%. The breadth of gains across memory, analog, and equipment sub-sectors suggested broad institutional rotation into the group.

briefs.headline: Software Stocks Bear the Brunt of Friday's Selling
briefs.body: The software sector fell 1.25% on Friday, weighed down by steep losses in automation and design names. Fair Isaac and UiPath each shed roughly 16.6%, while Autodesk dropped 8.26% and Snowflake lost 5.41%. The concentrated selling raises questions about whether enterprise software valuations are being reassessed ahead of upcoming earnings cycles.

briefs.headline: Gold Edges Up as Traders Await Inflation Figures
briefs.body: Bullion is ticking higher in pre-market trading as investors position cautiously ahead of U.S. inflation data due this week. The combination of elevated oil prices and geopolitical uncertainty is lending support to haven assets. A hotter-than-expected inflation reading could complicate the Federal Reserve's policy calculus and amplify cross-asset volatility.

briefs.headline: Australia Moves to Curb Algorithmic Social Media Feeds
briefs.body: Australian regulators published plans to allow social media users to opt out of algorithm-driven content feeds, delivering another regulatory blow to large technology platforms. The move follows similar discussions in Europe and could set a precedent for how democracies approach platform accountability. Broader tech-sector sentiment may face incremental headwinds if other markets adopt comparable frameworks.
